name: Ten Yard Fight
label: Equal Vision
lede: A Boston youth crew band whose singer showed up to the first show in football gear, that helped kick off hardcore's late-'90s youth crew revival, and that played its last show the same night the Red Sox were at Fenway in the playoffs.

eras.title: Shoulder pads and circle pits
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight started as something close to a joke: a straight edge band with a football theme and a singer in pads. The joke sold out its first 7" in under a week, and the band started taking itself seriously.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight's first show: Anthony Moreschi in football gear
years.p: Singer Anthony "Wrench" Moreschi plays Ten Yard Fight's first show in a mix of football gear and punk clothes. The crowd loves it, and the band starts playing up and down the East Coast.
Ten Yard Fight's first demo tape moves 1,000 copies, a real number for a new Boston hardcore band.
Ten Yard Fight's debut 7" on Boston's Big Wheel Recreation. According to Wikipedia the first pressing sold out in less than a week.
Ten Yard Fight share a 7" with Fastbreak. A CD collecting Demo '95 and Hardcore Pride follows.

eras.title: Back on track
eras.text: In 1997 Ten Yard Fight, In My Eyes and Floorpunch brought back the youth crew sound of the late '80s, and Equal Vision put out the record that led the charge. The band toured the US and Europe hard, and the line-up never sat still.

years.p: Ten Yard Fight's Equal Vision debut. Along with In My Eyes and Floorpunch, the band spearheads the 1997 youth crew revival.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight drummer Ben Chused doubles in [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]]
years.p: Ben Chused drums for Bane from 1997 to 1998, the band [[Aaron Dalbec|5ea0f2e5-66d0-48ce-82d5-9c85d2fa4c39]] started as a side project from [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]].

years.h: Ten Yard Fight tour Europe and the US, and swap members
years.p: Ten Yard Fight spend 1997 and 1998 touring Europe and the United States, with several line-up changes along the way.
Six new Ten Yard Fight songs on Equal Vision, their last studio release.

eras.title: Game day at the Karma Club
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight ended on a Boston Sunday with their friends on the bill and the Red Sox in the playoffs across the street. The date became a holiday.

years.p: Anthony Moreschi (vocals), John LaCroix (guitar, having started on bass), Tim Cossar (guitar), Brian "Clevo" Ristau (bass) and Ben Chused (drums).

years.h: Ten Yard Fight's last show, on Lansdowne Street during the ALCS
years.p: Ten Yard Fight play their final show at the Karma Club on Lansdowne Street, next to Fenway Park, the same day as that year's American League Championship Series. [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], Reach the Sky and [[In My Eyes|f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d]] play too.
years.xp: The show was later recognized as the first National Edge Day, and straight edge kids have marked the date ever since.

years.h: The Only Way: 1995–1999, a Ten Yard Fight video history
years.p: A documentary video of Ten Yard Fight's run comes out around 2000 as the band's final release.

years.h: Where Ten Yard Fight went: [[American Nightmare|f73634fa-c89b-4bc3-8cd0-81891bcafa9e]], Stand and Fight
years.p: Tim Cossar goes on to form American Nightmare. Anthony Moreschi fronts Stand and Fight on Bridge 9 and later Resist, with members of Drug Test and Since the Flood.

eras.title: Edge Day, every year
eras.text: The band that gave straight edge its holiday kept turning up on it. Moreschi and Ristau played as First and Ten, and the full band returned for This Is Hardcore.

years.h: First and Ten play National Edge Day in Haverhill
years.p: Anthony Moreschi and Brian Ristau reunite as First and Ten at National Edge Day 2007 in Haverhill, Massachusetts.

years.h: First and Ten share a bill with [[Slapshot|efc798e2-3165-49fd-a83b-d659cdb20488]]
years.p: Moreschi and Ristau's First and Ten play again, with Boston's Slapshot.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight headline night one of This Is Hardcore
years.p: Ten Yard Fight's original line-up reunites to headline the first day of This Is Hardcore 2018 in Philadelphia.
Wikipedia lists Ten Yard Fight as active again in 2025.
